title: Securing the AI Supply Chain: What Can We Learn From Developer-Reported Security Issues and Solutions of AI Projects?
role: later counterevidence that AI/model/data supply-chain dimensions are already being studied; narrows novelty
sections_checked: thematic analysis of 753 sampled posts and four themes
evidence_note: Reports 32 security issue and 24 solution categories across system/software, external tools/ecosystem, model, and data. It expands the construct space beyond conventional package dependencies. The 753 manually coded posts are a thematic sample, not a prevalence estimate.

title: Measuring the Security of the Evolving Software Supply Chain: a Research Agenda
role: current counterevidence that comparability, transitive dependencies, and real-world exploitability remain open; conceptual agenda, not empirical result
sections_checked: research questions on unified measurement, reachability, and AI-generated dependencies
conclusion and status of underlying SoK
evidence_note: Identifies ecosystem-specific measurement, transitive-dependency propagation/reachability, and AI-generated dependency patterns as current gaps. The paper is a research agenda and says its full SoK is under submission; do not treat proposed work as completed evidence.

title: Not All Dependencies are Equal: An Empirical Study on Production Dependencies in NPM
role: counterevidence that dependency risk depends on actual production/reachability context, not alert or manifest label alone
sections_checked: production dependency mapping across 100 npm projects
evidence_note: In 100 selected npm projects, the paper reports 98.1% of identified vulnerable dependencies were development dependencies and no npm audit alerts referred to production dependencies in that sample; it also warns that some development dependencies ship to production and that context-specific reachability is hard. This is not a general claim that development dependencies are safe.
